pull.title: KAFKA-20684 [7/N]: Point clients internals at RebalanceListener
pull.body:
Widens the private subscribeInternal helpers to RebalanceListener and
retargets internal javadoc, including StickyAssignor's worked examples.
Log strings now say RebalanceListener.onPartitionsX; no assertions
depend on them.

Reviewers: TengYao Chi <frankvicky@apache.org>, Chia-Ping Tsai
 <chia7712@gmail.com>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body:

Please merge the trunk also.

### 🟢 Approval recommended The private type widening preserves existing behavior, and the remaining documentation correction is non-blocking.
1 open issue - [Retain event class name when updating listener links](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23109#discussion_r4360619510) · New
What changed in this PR This PR continues the consumer migration to `RebalanceListener`, aligning private subscription helpers, documentation, and callback log names with the new interface. **Changes:** - Widen private subscription helper parameters to `RebalanceListener`. - Update listener documentation and StickyAssignor examples. - Use `RebalanceListener` in callback method log names. review_comments.body:
nit: this sentence now points readers at `subscribe(Collection, ConsumerRebalanceListener)` (the legacy overload, soon to be deprecated) to learn about the new `RebalanceListener`. Since this is the javadoc of the internal helper, maybe simply:

```suggestion
     * use of rebalance callbacks. Generally rebalances are triggered when there
```

and on the line above link to `{@link RebalanceListener}` (or `{@link #setRebalanceListener(RebalanceListener)}`) instead of the subscribe overload. The `@link`s at the top of this javadoc that mention `#subscribe(Pattern, ConsumerRebalanceListener)` are fine as-is, since that overload really is the caller of this helper.

nit: now that the example receives a `RebalanceConsumer consumer`, it could commit through it directly instead of the opaque `commitOffsets(partition)` helper, e.g. `consumer.commitSync(...)`. 
That would show the point of the new API. Same applies to `TheOldRebalanceListener` above.

RebalanceListener, and commit through the RebalanceConsumer in the
StickyAssignor examples.

repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
Drops the three subscribe(..., Optional<ConsumerRebalanceListener>)
overloads and the listener argument at all 52 call sites, all in
clients/src/test.

Reviewers: Chia-Ping Tsai <chia7712@gmail.com>

issue.title: KAFKA-20684 [9/N]: Deprecate ConsumerRebalanceListener for removal

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
Add a `@Deprecated` annotation on the now deprecated and uses removed (subscribe* methods on Consumer + ConsumerRebalanceListener) with forRemoval=true so future compilation would fail on the project, and log a loud warning on any clients using it.

Reviewers: Lianet Magrans <lmagrans@confluent.io>

issue.title: KAFKA-21292: Update docs of MockConsumer to use RebalanceListener

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
Update MockConsumer Javadocs to reference `RebalanceListener`

The Javadocs for `MockConsumer#losePartitions` referenced
`ConsumerRebalanceListener`, while the callbacks are handled by
`RebalanceListener`. Update the links to point to the correct listener
type.

Reviewers: Andrew Schofield <aschofield@confluent.io>
